concerns.text: T013 Step 4 triggers a 'reduced model' if row-wise missingness > 0.50 (5% of rows), whereas spec FR-009 mandates a reduced model only if missing covariates cause a sample drop >10%. The task logic silently relaxes the spec's 10% threshold to 5%, risking unnecessary covariate exclusion.

T013 Step 2 raises SystemExit(1) for any ID mismatch > 10%. Spec FR-009 distinguishes between 'halt' (core constructs missing) and 'proceed with reduced model' (covariates missing). The task treats all >10% drops as hard failures, violating the spec's conditional logic for covariate drops.

T023 calculates VIF and flags >5, but spec FR-005 and Edge Cases require an automatic corrective loop: if VIF > 5, the system MUST mean-center predictors and re-run diagnostics. The task lacks this mandatory remediation step, delivering a partial FR-005.

T013 Step 6 raises SystemExit(1) if core constructs are missing. Spec FR-008 requires the system to 'halt the analysis' with a structured log (`halt_log.json`). Raising an unhandled exception bypasses the required graceful halt state and logging, violating FR-008.

T029 generates a full cross-combination sweep (25 points), but T030 flags instability if CI crosses zero in >50% of *swept thresholds*. Spec SC-004 defines instability based on the 'defined threshold sweeps' (the specific 5 values per variable). The task's cross-combination dilutes the metric against the spec's intended definition.

T028 generates bootstrap CIs but lacks the logic to check if the primary effect is significant (p < 0.05) before applying the 'no crossing zero' stability check. Spec SC-002 explicitly conditions the stability requirement on the primary effect being significant.
